    mod = "dark " if l<0.3 else ("light " if l>0.7 else "")
    return mod+base

for i,(x0,x1,(r,g,b)) in enumerate(segs):
    pct0, pct1 = x0/W*100, x1/W*100
    print(f"{i:2d} x[{x0:4d}-{x1:4d}] {pct0:5.1f}-{pct1:5.1f}%  rgb=({r:3.0f},{g:3.0f},{b:3.0f})  {name_color(r,g,b)}")

"**Thunder**" is a song by American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons"). It was released by [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and [Kidinakorner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidinakorner "Kidinakorner") on April 27, 2017, as the second single from their third studio album, *[Evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolve_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Evolve (Imagine Dragons album)")* (2017).[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Written by band members [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds_\(singer\) "Dan Reynolds (singer)"), [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"), [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman"), and its producers [Alex Da Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Da_Kid "Alex Da Kid") and Jayson DeZuzio, "Thunder" peaked at number four, tying with "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")" on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100\.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") The song became the band's fourth single in that country to reach the top ten after "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")", "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")" and "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")". It also reached the top 10 in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Italy, New Zealand, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden and the Netherlands. The song was nominated for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Best Pop Duo/Group Performance").

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video for the song was released on Imagine Dragons' [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on May 2, 2017\. The video was shot in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), filmed in black and white.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It features the band's lead vocalist, [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), singing and dancing among extraterrestrials, portrayed by dancers Haroon Al Abdali, Mamadou Bathily, and Gianna Gi, around [Downtown Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dubai "Downtown Dubai") and the [Burj Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa"). It was directed by [Joseph Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kahn_\(director\) "Joseph Kahn (director)").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

As of October 2025, the video has over 2\.3 billion views on YouTube, making it the group's second most viewed video, only behind "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")". It also has over 13 million likes.

## Live performances

Ben McKee in 2013

Imagine Dragons performed the song at the [2017 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2017 "American Music Awards of 2017"), in a medley with singer [Khalid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalid_\(American_singer\) "Khalid (American singer)")'s "[Young Dumb & Broke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Dumb_&_Broke "Young Dumb & Broke")", with Khalid joining them for the performance.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) A little over a month later, on December 20, a studio version of the mash-up was released.[\[10\]](#cite_note-iTunes_Medley-10)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

"Thunder" peaked at number four on the US *Billboard* Hot 100\.[\[11\]](#cite_note-Peak-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-Hot_100-12) The single has also reached number one in Belarus, the Czech Republic and the top ten in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Netherlands, New Zealand, Paraguay, Poland, Russia, Slovakia, Sweden, and Switzerland. It topped the *Billboard* [Hot Rock Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_number-one_Billboard_Rock_Songs "List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs") chart for 21 weeks,[\[11\]](#cite_note-Peak-11)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) Alternative Songs (three weeks),[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Adult Top 40 (seven weeks), and the Mainstream Top 40 (for one week) charts.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Pop_Songs-15)

It became the ninth best-selling song of 2017 in the United States, with 1,189,000 copies sold in the year.[\[16\]](#cite_note-us_sales-16)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Critics from *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* magazine placed the song at number 84 on its list of best songs of 2017, stating "'Thunder' is relatively stripped down, and between its soldierly cadence and a bouncy, helium-inflated, one-word hook, it makes for a curious pop gem".[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) In a review of the band's live performance at London's [O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O2_Arena_\(London\) "O2 Arena (London)"), *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* wrote of the song: "...the irresistible, hiccupping electro-pop of Thunder, a tune that could sit equally happily in a set by [Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)") or [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna")".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

"**Thunder**" is a song by American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons"). It was released by [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and [Kidinakorner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidinakorner "Kidinakorner") on April 27, 2017, as the second single from their third studio album, *[Evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolve_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Evolve (Imagine Dragons album)")* (2017).[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Written by band members [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds_\(singer\) "Dan Reynolds (singer)"), [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"), [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman"), and its producers [Alex Da Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Da_Kid "Alex Da Kid") and Jayson DeZuzio, "Thunder" peaked at number four, tying with "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")" on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100\.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") The song became the band's fourth single in that country to reach the top ten after "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")", "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")" and "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")". It also reached the top 10 in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Italy, New Zealand, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden and the Netherlands. The song was nominated for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Best Pop Duo/Group Performance").

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video for the song was released on Imagine Dragons' [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on May 2, 2017\. The video was shot in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), filmed in black and white.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It features the band's lead vocalist, [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), singing and dancing among extraterrestrials, portrayed by dancers Haroon Al Abdali, Mamadou Bathily, and Gianna Gi, around [Downtown Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dubai "Downtown Dubai") and the [Burj Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa"). It was directed by [Joseph Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kahn_\(director\) "Joseph Kahn (director)").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

As of October 2025, the video has over 2\.3 billion views on YouTube, making it the group's second most viewed video, only behind "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")". It also has over 13 million likes.

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

"Thunder" peaked at number four on the US *Billboard* Hot 100\.[\[11\]](#cite_note-Peak-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-Hot_100-12) The single has also reached number one in Belarus, the Czech Republic and the top ten in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Netherlands, New Zealand, Paraguay, Poland, Russia, Slovakia, Sweden, and Switzerland. It topped the *Billboard* [Hot Rock Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_number-one_Billboard_Rock_Songs "List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs") chart for 21 weeks,[\[11\]](#cite_note-Peak-11)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) Alternative Songs (three weeks),[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Adult Top 40 (seven weeks), and the Mainstream Top 40 (for one week) charts.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Pop_Songs-15)

It became the ninth best-selling song of 2017 in the United States, with 1,189,000 copies sold in the year.[\[16\]](#cite_note-us_sales-16)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Critics from *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* magazine placed the song at number 84 on its list of best songs of 2017, stating "'Thunder' is relatively stripped down, and between its soldierly cadence and a bouncy, helium-inflated, one-word hook, it makes for a curious pop gem".[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) In a review of the band's live performance at London's [O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O2_Arena_\(London\) "O2 Arena (London)"), *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* wrote of the song: "...the irresistible, hiccupping electro-pop of Thunder, a tune that could sit equally happily in a set by [Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)") or [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna")".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

"**This Is What You Came For**" is a song by Scottish DJ and record producer [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") featuring Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna"). Released as a standalone single on 29 April 2016, by [Sony Music UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_UK "Sony Music UK") and Westbury Road, the song was included on Harris' first [compilation album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"), *[96 Months](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96_Months "96 Months")* (2024). Harris wrote the song with American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), who was initially credited under the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") Nils Sjöberg. Production was handled by Harris and [Kuk Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuk_Harrell "Kuk Harrell"). The song marked Rihanna and Harris's second collaboration, following "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" (2011).

The single debuted at number two on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"). It peaked at number three on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Rihanna's 21st top-five song and Harris's second; the song is currently Harris's highest-peaking single as a lead artist in the US. It became Rihanna's 25th and Harris's fourth chart-topper on the [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") and also reached number one on the US [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Dance/Electronic_Songs "Hot Dance/Electronic Songs"); the single became the 12th number one for Rihanna and Harris's tenth on the sister chart [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay"). It topped the charts in 12 countries including Australia, Canada and Ireland, and peaked within the top ten in France, Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, New Zealand and Switzerland. A music video for the song premiered on 17 June 2016 and features Rihanna in an open cube with images projected on the inside walls.

## Writing and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and release")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg)

[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") (pictured in 2015) wrote the lyrics for "This Is What You Came For", but was initially credited under the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg. The song also features Swift's uncredited backing vocals.

[Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") presented the final recording to Rihanna, two weeks prior to its release. During his performance at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella"), Harris shared the song with Rihanna and her manager in her trailer. Harris stated that he was "nervous" to play her the song because he had "changed so many bits from when she first heard it."[\[2\]](#cite_note-3) The song was released on 29 April 2016\. The song marks the pair's third collaboration, following the global chart-topper "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" and the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") top-five single "[Where Have You Been](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Have_You_Been "Where Have You Been")", which are both featured on Rihanna's sixth studio album, *[Talk That Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_That_Talk "Talk That Talk")* (2011).[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4)

> I think, when a pseudonym comes in is when you still have a love for making the work and you don't want the work to become overshadowed by this thing that's been built around you, based on what people know about you. And that's when it's really fun to create fake names and write under them. I wrote under the name Nils Sjöberg because those are two of the most popular names of Swedish males. I wrote this song called "This Is What You Came For" that Rihanna ended up singing. And nobody knew for a while. I remembered always hearing that when [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_\(singer\) "Prince (singer)") wrote "[Manic Monday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manic_Monday "Manic Monday")", they didn't reveal it for a couple of months.

— Swift on penning the song, *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*[\[4\]](#cite_note-5)

Harris and Nils Sjöberg were credited as songwriters and producers. On 13 July 2016 however, TMZ reported that the track was written by Harris's then-girlfriend, American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), who used the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg because they did not want their relationship to overshadow the song.[\[5\]](#cite_note-tmz-6)[\[6\]](#cite_note-7) The track became a point of contention upon its release when Harris—in response to being asked about the possibility of collaborating with Swift during an interview with [Ryan Seacrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Seacrest "Ryan Seacrest")—said that he "can't see it happening."[\[5\]](#cite_note-tmz-6) Harris eventually confirmed on his Twitter account that Swift wrote the lyrics and contributed some background vocals, while he "wrote the music, produced the song, arranged it and cut \[Rihanna's\] vocals". He also confirmed Swift's previous request for secrecy as co-writer.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Nils-8) The credit has since been officially changed to "Taylor Swift" in [BMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Music,_Inc. "Broadcast Music, Inc.")'s and [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s entry for the song.[\[8\]](#cite_note-bmi-9)[\[9\]](#cite_note-ASCAP-10)

On 1 March 2023, various unreleased songs of Swift's [leaked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_leak "Music leak") online, including her full original demo recording of "This Is What You Came For".[\[10\]](#cite_note-11)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_%28Cropped%29.png/250px-Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_%28Cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_\(Cropped\).png)

"This is What You Came For" marks Rihanna's second collaboration with Harris, following 2011's "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")".

"This Is What You Came For" is an [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") and [Eurodance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurodance "Eurodance") song.[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4)[\[11\]](#cite_note-12)[\[12\]](#cite_note-idolator.com-13) Gil Kaufman of *Billboard* stated that the song is "a chilled-out, joyful club track that nods to classic [Chicago house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_house "Chicago house") from the late 1980s and early 1990s, but with a modern, poppier flavor."[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4) The song is written in the key of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 124 beats per minute. The song follows a chord progression of Am–Fmaj7–G–C, and Rihanna's vocals span from G3 to E5, amounting to 2 different octaves.[\[13\]](#cite_note-14)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")\]

### Critical

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical")\]

"This Is What You Came For" received generally positive reviews. Lary Barleet from *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")* stated that "As it builds to a climax, he pulls it right back, eschewing the [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") [drop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDM_drop "EDM drop") in favour of voguish and mellow [tropical house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_house "Tropical house"). It will definitely be a hit, however by manipulating her voice so much he's stripped away the personality that made '[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")' such a standout, and her latest album *[Anti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti_\(album\) "Anti (album)")* so compelling. The result is surprisingly soulless."[\[14\]](#cite_note-nme.com-15) Robbie Daw from the *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")* gave the song a positive review, stating, "The song is pretty decent [Euro-centric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro-centric "Euro-centric") dance floor fodder. It's just a bit subdued-which might have been the correct decision; why attempt to top a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") classic and fail when you can zig left, aiming for other territory altogether?"[\[12\]](#cite_note-idolator.com-13)

### Commercial

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial")\]

"This Is What You Came For" debuted at number two on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"). The single debuted at number nine on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on May 21, 2016, eventually peaking at number three on the chart on August 6, 2016, becoming Rihanna's 28th top ten hit in the US, Harris's fourth, while on the magazine's [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") it extended Rihanna's number-one streak on that chart to 12 (the most of any artist on that chart) and gave Harris his tenth (the most among male artists, but at the same time extended his most weeks at number one on the chart among artists to 73).[\[15\]](#cite_note-16) "This Is What You Came For" became Rihanna's 25th and Harris's fourth number one on the [Hot Dance Club Songs Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs"), where it became the first song since 2013's "[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\) "Wake Me Up (Avicii song)")" to stay at number one for two weeks.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) As of October 2016, the single has sold 1\.2 million copies in the United States.[\[17\]](#cite_note-ussales-18)

"This Is What You Came For" debuted at number one on the [Scottish Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Singles_Chart "Scottish Singles Chart"), and peaked at number one in Australia, Canada and Ireland. The song also reached the top 10 in Germany, Ireland, New Zealand, Switzerland, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Hungary, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal and Slovakia. The song has reached the top 10 in all except three of the countries it has charted in.

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video for the song directed by [Emil Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Nava "Emil Nava") with Director of Photography Martin Coppen, edited by Ellie Johnson, post production creative and 3D environments by Chris Hoffman, and produced and projection mapped by Matt Brown, was released to [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") on 16 June 2016\. In it, a giant white box is shown sitting in a variety of places, such as a misty field and a forest. The scene then cuts to Rihanna, dressed in a sparkly blue jumpsuit, singing while standing and dancing inside the box. While she performs, graphics are projected onto all 5 sides around her. Lasers were the only other effects used with the video projections, and were provided by Dynamic FX. These include a variety of video effects and designs, footage of a crowd partying and running horses, and a drawing of a mountain with lightning over it. The video technology used for projections blended all angles of the backing video, so it would be displayed without skewing the image and allowing it to play back in a 3D environment. This new technology was being used for the first time on this video. This video also had many scenes and different cube designs cut from it, as the filming was cut short due to time constrains. Calvin Harris makes a brief cameo appearance in the video, driving a sports car ([Lamborghini Aventador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_Aventador "Lamborghini Aventador")).[\[18\]](#cite_note-19) As the video ends, Rihanna walks outside, revealing the box has been set up on a dark, deserted soundstage. Two months after its release, the video reached 500 million views, and on 29 November 2016, the video reached one billion views. As of September 2025, it has reached 2\.8 billion views, and is [the site's 66th most viewed video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[19\]](#cite_note-20)

"**This Is What You Came For**" is a song by Scottish DJ and record producer [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") featuring Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna"). Released as a standalone single on 29 April 2016, by [Sony Music UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_UK "Sony Music UK") and Westbury Road, the song was included on Harris' first [compilation album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"), *[96 Months](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96_Months "96 Months")* (2024). Harris wrote the song with American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), who was initially credited under the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") Nils Sjöberg. Production was handled by Harris and [Kuk Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuk_Harrell "Kuk Harrell"). The song marked Rihanna and Harris's second collaboration, following "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" (2011).

The single debuted at number two on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"). It peaked at number three on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Rihanna's 21st top-five song and Harris's second; the song is currently Harris's highest-peaking single as a lead artist in the US. It became Rihanna's 25th and Harris's fourth chart-topper on the [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") and also reached number one on the US [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Dance/Electronic_Songs "Hot Dance/Electronic Songs"); the single became the 12th number one for Rihanna and Harris's tenth on the sister chart [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay"). It topped the charts in 12 countries including Australia, Canada and Ireland, and peaked within the top ten in France, Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, New Zealand and Switzerland. A music video for the song premiered on 17 June 2016 and features Rihanna in an open cube with images projected on the inside walls.

## Writing and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and release")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg/250px-Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taylor_Swift_May_2015_cropped_and_retouched.jpg)

[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") (pictured in 2015) wrote the lyrics for "This Is What You Came For", but was initially credited under the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg. The song also features Swift's uncredited backing vocals.

[Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") presented the final recording to Rihanna, two weeks prior to its release. During his performance at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella"), Harris shared the song with Rihanna and her manager in her trailer. Harris stated that he was "nervous" to play her the song because he had "changed so many bits from when she first heard it."[\[2\]](#cite_note-3) The song was released on 29 April 2016\. The song marks the pair's third collaboration, following the global chart-topper "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" and the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") top-five single "[Where Have You Been](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_Have_You_Been "Where Have You Been")", which are both featured on Rihanna's sixth studio album, *[Talk That Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_That_Talk "Talk That Talk")* (2011).[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4)

> I think, when a pseudonym comes in is when you still have a love for making the work and you don't want the work to become overshadowed by this thing that's been built around you, based on what people know about you. And that's when it's really fun to create fake names and write under them. I wrote under the name Nils Sjöberg because those are two of the most popular names of Swedish males. I wrote this song called "This Is What You Came For" that Rihanna ended up singing. And nobody knew for a while. I remembered always hearing that when [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_\(singer\) "Prince (singer)") wrote "[Manic Monday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manic_Monday "Manic Monday")", they didn't reveal it for a couple of months.

— Swift on penning the song, *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*[\[4\]](#cite_note-5)

Harris and Nils Sjöberg were credited as songwriters and producers. On 13 July 2016 however, TMZ reported that the track was written by Harris's then-girlfriend, American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"), who used the pseudonym Nils Sjöberg because they did not want their relationship to overshadow the song.[\[5\]](#cite_note-tmz-6)[\[6\]](#cite_note-7) The track became a point of contention upon its release when Harris—in response to being asked about the possibility of collaborating with Swift during an interview with [Ryan Seacrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Seacrest "Ryan Seacrest")—said that he "can't see it happening."[\[5\]](#cite_note-tmz-6) Harris eventually confirmed on his Twitter account that Swift wrote the lyrics and contributed some background vocals, while he "wrote the music, produced the song, arranged it and cut \[Rihanna's\] vocals". He also confirmed Swift's previous request for secrecy as co-writer.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Nils-8) The credit has since been officially changed to "Taylor Swift" in [BMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Music,_Inc. "Broadcast Music, Inc.")'s and [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s entry for the song.[\[8\]](#cite_note-bmi-9)[\[9\]](#cite_note-ASCAP-10)

On 1 March 2023, various unreleased songs of Swift's [leaked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_leak "Music leak") online, including her full original demo recording of "This Is What You Came For".[\[10\]](#cite_note-11)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_%28Cropped%29.png/250px-Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_%28Cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rihanna_Diamonds_World_Tour_2013_\(Cropped\).png)

"This is What You Came For" marks Rihanna's second collaboration with Harris, following 2011's "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")".

"This Is What You Came For" is an [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") and [Eurodance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurodance "Eurodance") song.[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4)[\[11\]](#cite_note-12)[\[12\]](#cite_note-idolator.com-13) Gil Kaufman of *Billboard* stated that the song is "a chilled-out, joyful club track that nods to classic [Chicago house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_house "Chicago house") from the late 1980s and early 1990s, but with a modern, poppier flavor."[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-4) The song is written in the key of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 124 beats per minute. The song follows a chord progression of Am–Fmaj7–G–C, and Rihanna's vocals span from G3 to E5, amounting to 2 different octaves.[\[13\]](#cite_note-14)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")\]

### Critical

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical")\]

"This Is What You Came For" received generally positive reviews. Lary Barleet from *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")* stated that "As it builds to a climax, he pulls it right back, eschewing the [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") [drop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDM_drop "EDM drop") in favour of voguish and mellow [tropical house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_house "Tropical house"). It will definitely be a hit, however by manipulating her voice so much he's stripped away the personality that made '[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")' such a standout, and her latest album *[Anti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti_\(album\) "Anti (album)")* so compelling. The result is surprisingly soulless."[\[14\]](#cite_note-nme.com-15) Robbie Daw from the *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")* gave the song a positive review, stating, "The song is pretty decent [Euro-centric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro-centric "Euro-centric") dance floor fodder. It's just a bit subdued-which might have been the correct decision; why attempt to top a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") classic and fail when you can zig left, aiming for other territory altogether?"[\[12\]](#cite_note-idolator.com-13)

### Commercial

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial")\]

"This Is What You Came For" debuted at number two on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"). The single debuted at number nine on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on May 21, 2016, eventually peaking at number three on the chart on August 6, 2016, becoming Rihanna's 28th top ten hit in the US, Harris's fourth, while on the magazine's [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") it extended Rihanna's number-one streak on that chart to 12 (the most of any artist on that chart) and gave Harris his tenth (the most among male artists, but at the same time extended his most weeks at number one on the chart among artists to 73).[\[15\]](#cite_note-16) "This Is What You Came For" became Rihanna's 25th and Harris's fourth number one on the [Hot Dance Club Songs Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs"), where it became the first song since 2013's "[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\) "Wake Me Up (Avicii song)")" to stay at number one for two weeks.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) As of October 2016, the single has sold 1\.2 million copies in the United States.[\[17\]](#cite_note-ussales-18)

"This Is What You Came For" debuted at number one on the [Scottish Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Singles_Chart "Scottish Singles Chart"), and peaked at number one in Australia, Canada and Ireland. The song also reached the top 10 in Germany, Ireland, New Zealand, Switzerland, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Hungary, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal and Slovakia. The song has reached the top 10 in all except three of the countries it has charted in.

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=This_Is_What_You_Came_For&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video for the song directed by [Emil Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Nava "Emil Nava") with Director of Photography Martin Coppen, edited by Ellie Johnson, post production creative and 3D environments by Chris Hoffman, and produced and projection mapped by Matt Brown, was released to [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") on 16 June 2016\. In it, a giant white box is shown sitting in a variety of places, such as a misty field and a forest. The scene then cuts to Rihanna, dressed in a sparkly blue jumpsuit, singing while standing and dancing inside the box. While she performs, graphics are projected onto all 5 sides around her. Lasers were the only other effects used with the video projections, and were provided by Dynamic FX. These include a variety of video effects and designs, footage of a crowd partying and running horses, and a drawing of a mountain with lightning over it. The video technology used for projections blended all angles of the backing video, so it would be displayed without skewing the image and allowing it to play back in a 3D environment. This new technology was being used for the first time on this video. This video also had many scenes and different cube designs cut from it, as the filming was cut short due to time constrains. Calvin Harris makes a brief cameo appearance in the video, driving a sports car ([Lamborghini Aventador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_Aventador "Lamborghini Aventador")).[\[18\]](#cite_note-19) As the video ends, Rihanna walks outside, revealing the box has been set up on a dark, deserted soundstage. Two months after its release, the video reached 500 million views, and on 29 November 2016, the video reached one billion views. As of September 2025, it has reached 2\.8 billion views, and is [the site's 66th most viewed video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[19\]](#cite_note-20)
